title: Chiranjit Das
text:
About
I am a postdoctoral researcher at the Laboratoire des Sciences du Climat et de l’Environnement (LSCE). My interests are in remote sensing and inversion methodologies to understand the distribution of GHG fluxes across spheres. It sits at the intersection of satellite observation, atmospheric modeling, and GHG cycle science, aiming to close gaps in how we observe and attribute GHG sources and sinks at regional and global scales.

title: Research
text:
My research focus on quantifying and understanding CO2 fluxes across the atmosphere-biosphere-ocean system, combining satellite remote sensing with inverse modeling techniques.

Remote Sensing & Inversion of CO2 Fluxes
I use satellite-derived trace gas retrievals together with atmospheric transport and inversion frameworks to estimate surface CO2 fluxes and constrain their spatial and temporal distribution.


Carbon Cycle Processes
Investigating the drivers of terrestrial and oceanic carbon uptake and release, and how these processes respond to climate variability.


Greenhouse Gas Dynamics at Regional Scales
Studying the regional-scale distribution and variability of CO2, CH4, and N2O, and their links to land-use, emissions, and natural sink/source processes.


Carbon-Climate Interactions & Global Warming
Examining feedbacks between the carbon cycle and the climate system, and how these interactions shape projections of future warming.
